page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 372 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core and multi-core capabilities. Geekbench single-core, image processing, and text processing benchmarks rank in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also achieves top-tier performance, while multi-threaded decompression and software compilation with Clang register in the strong top 25% category. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large-block read and write operations fall into the average tier. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models and strong prompt processing speeds with medium 7B models.

From a resource density perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the overhead of additional compute cores. However, the absence of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which represents a potential I/O latency tradeoff. The instance delivers average performance in database operations and Redis SET benchmarks, indicating it is optimized more for memory-intensive processing and vector calculations than high-throughput transactional database writes.

The hardware profile and benchmark results make this instance suitable for memory-intensive applications, software compilation, text and image processing pipelines, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference tasks. It is also applicable for static web serving and memory-bound analytical workloads that leverage its AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets.
